record.original_question: Extend Thurston’s combinatorial theory of critically finite rational maps, where the post-critical set P is finite, to all geometrically finite rational maps. That is, describe such a map f up to combinatorial equivalence relative to P by finite topological data, and characterize which combinatorial types are realized by rational maps.

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Extend Thurston’s combinatorial theory of critical finite rational maps (those for which |P | < ∞) to all geometrically finite maps. That is, describe f up to combinatorial equivalence rel P by a finite amount of topological data, and characterize those combinatorial types which arise as rational maps.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ be a rational map of degree at least two on the Riemann sphere. Let $C_f$ denote the set of critical points of $f$, and let
$$P_f = \overline{\bigcup_{n\geq 1} f^n(C_f)}$$
be the post-critical set. The map $f$ is called critically finite (post-critically finite) if $P_f$ is finite, and geometrically finite if $P_f \cap J(f)$ is finite, where $J(f)$ is the Julia set (equivalently, every critical point in $J(f)$ has a finite forward orbit, while critical points in the Fatou set may have infinite orbits contained in attracting basins).

Two branched coverings $f,g:S^2\to S^2$ with marked sets $P_f, P_g$ are combinatorially equivalent rel $P$ if there exist orientation-preserving homeomorphisms $\varphi_0,\varphi_1:(S^2,P_f)\to(S^2,P_g)$ with $\varphi_0\circ f=g\circ\varphi_1$ and $\varphi_0$ isotopic to $\varphi_1$ rel $P_f$.

Thurston's theorem classifies critically finite rational maps up to combinatorial equivalence by finite topological data (a critically finite branched self-cover of $S^2$ together with the marked post-critical set), and characterizes which such combinatorial classes are realized by rational maps via the absence of a Thurston obstruction.

Problem: Extend Thurston's combinatorial theory to all geometrically finite rational maps. Specifically:
(a) Define a notion of finite topological data describing a geometrically finite rational map up to combinatorial equivalence rel $P_f$, allowing for critical points with infinite orbits in attracting Fatou components.
(b) Determine necessary and sufficient combinatorial conditions on such topological data so that the corresponding combinatorial class is realized by a geometrically finite rational map on $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress has been made. Cui, Jiang, and Sullivan extended Thurston's characterization to sub-hyperbolic semi-rational branched coverings, and Cui–Tan gave a characterization of hyperbolic rational maps via similar combinatorial obstructions. Further extensions cover rational maps with disconnected Julia sets and parabolic orbifolds. However, a complete combinatorial classification covering all geometrically finite rational maps (including the parabolic cycles case in full generality) does not appear to be fully settled as a single uniform theorem.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorial characterization of sub-hyperbolic rational maps
status_evidence.snippet: This criterion was extended by Cui, Jiang, and Sullivan to sub-hyperbolic rational maps among sub-hyperbolic semi-rational branched coverings of S^2.
status_evidence.claim: Sub-hyperbolic case (a subclass of geometrically finite) is solved.

status_evidence.title: A characterization of hyperbolic rational maps
status_evidence.snippet: Thurston's theory extended to rational maps with infinite critical orbits assuming hyperbolicity, with concrete obstruction criteria.
status_evidence.claim: Hyperbolic geometrically finite case has been characterized combinatorially.

status_evidence.title: Thurston type Theorem for sub-hyperbolic rational maps
status_evidence.snippet: Thurston-type theorem extended to sub-hyperbolic rational maps.
status_evidence.claim: Significant partial extension toward the geometrically finite setting.
